title: Spec of a universal square-zero thickening of rings is a universal first order thickening of affine schemes
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $\pi:S'\to S$ be a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras whose kernel $K$ satisfies $K^2=0$ and which has the following universal property: for every $R$-algebra $A$, every ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$ (quotient map $q:A\to A/I$) and every $R$-algebra map $a:S\to A/I$, there is exactly one $R$-algebra map $a':S'\to A$ with $q\circ a'=a\circ\pi$. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S$, $Z'=\operatorname{Spec}S'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $h=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:Z\to X$, $i=\operatorname{Spec}\pi:Z\to Z'$ and $h'=\operatorname{Spec}(R\to S'):Z'\to X$. Then $i$ is a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf has square zero, $h'\circ i=h$, and $Z\subset Z'$ (with $h'$) is a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]: the universal property holds for all first order thickenings $T\subset T'$ over $X$, with $T'$ an arbitrary (not necessarily affine) scheme.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), third paragraph ('Before we glue affine pieces ... Thus the lemma holds if X and Z are affine'): the universal property for affine T, T' from Algebra, Lemma 04EB, then for general T' by an affine open covering of T' and glueing of the morphisms
